fact: x86-64 Linux: number in rax, arguments in rdi rsi rdx r10 r8 r9, instruction `syscall`
rax holds the result; values from -4095 to -1 are -errno
`syscall` destroys rcx and r11; all other registers are preserved
SysV AMD64 function call: integer or pointer arguments in rdi rsi rdx rcx r8 r9, then the stack
SysV AMD64: integer result in rax (rdx for the second half of a 128-bit value)
SysV AMD64 callee-saved: rbx rbp r12 r13 r14 r15 (and rsp)
SysV AMD64 caller-saved: rax rcx rdx rsi rdi r8 r9 r10 r11 and all vector registers
rsp is 16-byte aligned immediately before a `call` (so rsp+8 is 16-byte aligned at function entry)
128 bytes below rsp are usable by a leaf function without adjusting rsp
A static NASM program starts at _start with no return address: it must end with the exit or exit_group syscall
nasm -f elf64 prog.asm && ld -o prog prog.o builds a static Linux x86-64 executable
